rationale: All three review lenses ran cleanly against the backend-only diff for EPMCDME-10930 (frontend changes in the spec are out of scope for this repo). Five blocking findings survive triage: GET /v1/admin/users/{id} silently returns an authorized-but-empty projects list for pure auditors (CR-002, critical — violates the required 'view per-user detail' criterion), POST /v1/admin/users silently drops a requested is_auditor=true (CR-003), the new is_auditor repository filter is silently skipped when combined with platform_role+projects filters (CR-001), the Alembic down_revision was not verified against the live head as spec section 2.2 explicitly required (CR-004 — the follow-up merge migration does resolve to a single head, so this is a process gap rather than a live break), and required section 5.2 test coverage (auditor 200s on most read endpoints, 403 on all write endpoints, and the PUT assignment authorization matrix) is missing (CR-005) — exactly the gap that let CR-002 ship undetected. Roughly a dozen additional observations (log-domain mislabeling in the new auth dependency, inconsistent getattr-vs-direct is_auditor access, stale docstrings, a missing DB index, an unrelated bundled enforce_limit budget fix, and speculative concerns that were independently confirmed as matching the approved spec design) were reviewed and dismissed as non-blocking or already correctly handled.

findings.title: is_auditor filter dropped by early-return filter branches
findings.problem: _apply_filters() early-returns at lines 690 and 692 when platform_role is PLATFORM_ADMIN or USER together with a non-empty projects filter, before the new is_auditor check at lines 721-722 ever runs.
findings.impact: An admin combining an is_auditor filter with platform_role=user/platform_admin and a projects filter in the Users Management UI gets results that silently ignore the is_auditor constraint, returning the wrong user list.
findings.recommendation: Apply the is_auditor (and pre-existing budgets) filter before the platform_role+projects early-return branches, or replicate the is_auditor where-clause inside _apply_platform_admin_project_filter/_apply_user_project_filter.

findings.title: Pure auditor gets empty projects list on user detail
findings.problem: get_user() computes is_project_admin = user.is_applications_admin and not user.is_admin_or_maintainer and passes user.is_admin_or_maintainer as is_admin; neither expression accounts for is_auditor, so a pure auditor (is_admin=False, is_maintainer=False, is_applications_admin=False) yields is_admin=False and is_project_admin=False.
findings.impact: get_user_with_relationships() (user_management_service.py:185-187) falls into its 'regular users should not reach here' else branch and returns projects=[], even though the auditor is correctly authorized past project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access — silently violating the spec's required 'view ... per-user detail' criterion.
findings.recommendation: Pass is_admin=user.is_admin_or_maintainer or getattr(user, 'is_auditor', False) (mirroring the pattern used elsewhere in this diff) so auditors take the is_admin branch and see all projects.

findings.title: POST /v1/admin/users silently drops requested is_auditor
findings.problem: create_user() calls create_local_user_with_flow(..., is_admin=data.is_admin, is_maintainer=data.is_maintainer, ...) without forwarding data.is_auditor; create_local_user and create_local_user_with_flow (user_management_service.py:71-79, 555-563) have no is_auditor parameter at all.
findings.impact: A caller creating a user with is_auditor=true in the request body gets a 200 response, but the new user is always persisted with is_auditor=False — a silently dropped field on a DTO the spec explicitly added is_auditor to.
findings.recommendation: Add is_auditor: bool = False to create_local_user and create_local_user_with_flow, thread it into the UserDB(...) construction, and pass data.is_auditor from the router.

findings.title: Migration down_revision not verified against live head before authoring
findings.problem: down_revision is hardcoded to 't1u2v3w4x5y6', the spec's assumed placeholder, but that revision already had a sibling child on main (9b9b4c585e54) — it was not actually the current head when this migration was authored, exactly the branch-fork failure mode spec section 2.2 explicitly warned against.
findings.impact: Required an unplanned second migration (1bd75582b209_merge_auditor_and_lifecycle_heads.py) to reconcile the resulting two heads. The net result does resolve to a single head, but the prescribed verify-before-authoring step was skipped, and a future rebase could reintroduce the same fork if not re-verified.
findings.recommendation: Run `alembic heads` on the final branch state before merge to confirm exactly one head, and document why the merge migration was needed (or squash the two migrations into one with the correct down_revision).

findings.title: Missing required auditor test coverage per spec section 5.2
findings.problem: Spec section 5.2 requires pure-auditor-fixture 200 tests on GET /v1/admin/users/{id}, .../projects, .../knowledge-bases, .../budgets, GET /v1/projects, GET /v1/projects/{name}?include_spending=true, GET /v1/projects/{name}/spends, and 5 of the 6 analytics guards (only the line-593 _authorize_admin_budget_view guard is tested); it also requires 403 write-rejection tests for a pure auditor on every listed write endpoint (none exist), and a caller-role authorization matrix for PUT /v1/admin/users/{id} is_auditor assignment (the only existing test calls the service layer directly, bypassing the admin_access_only router guard).
findings.impact: This is exactly the coverage gap that let CR-002 (empty projects for auditor) ship undetected; the write-rejection and assignment-matrix gaps leave the feature's core security guarantee (auditor cannot write) and its only privileged-write path unverified by CI.
findings.recommendation: Add the router-level (not just helper-level) test matrix spec section 5.2 describes: pure-auditor 200s on each listed GET route, pure-auditor 403s on each listed write route, and admin/maintainer/auditor-caller assertions for PUT .../is_auditor assignment.
